metadata.description: Giovanni's personal collection of agent skills — Neovim/Lua API references, Anki card generation, test-first planning and regression testing, terminal-demo recording, NixOS homelab operations, and third-party skill adoption.

plugins.name: nvim
plugins.description: Reference for Neovim's Lua API surface (vim.api, vim.fn, and builtin helpers such as vim.schedule, vim.wait, vim.ui_*). Use when writing or editing Neovim Lua plugins/configs, or when an agent needs exact vim.api/vim.fn signatures.

plugins.name: nvim.diagnostics
plugins.description: Reference for vim.diagnostic and diagnostic-namespace APIs in Neovim Lua (signs, virtual text/lines, goto next/prev, qf/loclist, enable/disable). Use when implementing diagnostics display or navigation.

plugins.name: nvim.lsp
plugins.description: Reference for vim.lsp, vim.lsp.buf, vim.lsp.util, vim.lsp.codelens, vim.lsp.semantic_tokens, and the LSP protocol APIs in Neovim Lua. Use when wiring language-server features (hover, definitions, references, code actions, formatting, completion, inlay hints).

plugins.name: nvim.treesitter
plugins.description: Reference for Neovim treesitter Lua APIs (TSNode, TSTree, TSQuery, TSParser, query cursors). Use when writing tree-sitter queries, node traversal, or syntax-aware edits.

plugins.name: nvim.loop
plugins.description: Reference for vim.loop / vim.uv (libuv) bindings in Neovim Lua — timers, spawned processes, filesystem, streams/pipes, OS queries, and handle lifecycle. Use when writing async I/O, timers, job runners, or file watchers.

plugins.name: nvim.keymap
plugins.description: Reference for vim.keymap in Neovim Lua (set/del and mapping options). Use when creating, modifying, or removing key mappings, buffer-local maps, or callback mappings.

plugins.name: nvim.fs
plugins.description: Reference for vim.fs in Neovim Lua — path joining, dirname/basename/ext, normalization, mkdir/rm, find, and directory/parent iterators. Use when manipulating file paths or walking directories.

plugins.name: nvim.utility
plugins.description: Reference for the miscellaneous vim.* helpers in Neovim Lua not covered by the other nvim skills — table helpers, json/mpack, inspect, iter, version, notify/log, string utils, validate/defer, options accessors, vim.system, vim.snippet, vim.highlight, and vim.ui. Use for general-purpose Lua helpers when writing plugins.

plugins.name: nvim.snippet
plugins.description: Reference for vim.snippet in Neovim Lua (expand/jump/active/stop). Use when implementing or driving LSP/extensible snippet expansion and tabstop navigation in plugins or configs.

plugins.name: nvim.system
plugins.description: Reference for vim.system in Neovim Lua — the libuv-backed process runner (0.10+). Use when spawning external commands, capturing output, or controlling child processes as an alternative to jobstart for simple cases.

plugins.name: prime-planning
plugins.description: Plan feature work with an appropriate verification strategy; use when a feature plan is requested.

plugins.name: regression-testing
plugins.description: Choose and run regression checks for a change or investigate a regression.

plugins.name: luasnip
plugins.description: Reference for the LuaSnip snippet-engine API (require('luasnip')) — node constructors (s/sn/t/i/f/c/d/r), snippet opts (trig/wordTrig/regTrig/snippetType/condition/callbacks), events, add_snippets, and extras (fmt/rep/lambda/match). Use when authoring, editing, or debugging LuaSnip snippets and autosnippets.

plugins.name: anki.note-types
plugins.description: Anki's data model — notes vs cards, fields, note types, and the built-in types (Basic, Basic (and reversed), Basic (optional reversed), Basic (type in the answer), Cloze, Image Occlusion). Covers card-generation rules, deck override, and tags. Use when designing note types or deciding how cards are generated from notes.

plugins.name: anki.card-templates
plugins.description: Anki card template language — field replacement {{Field}}, conditionals {{#Field}}/{{^Field}}, special fields ({{Tags}}, {{FrontSide}}, {{Type}}, {{Deck}}, {{Subdeck}}, {{CardFlag}}, {{Card}}), filters (type:, cloze:, text:, hint:, tts:, furigana:/kana:/kanji:, cloze-only:), the {{FrontSide}} + <hr id=answer> divider, raw HTML/CSS, and card-generation rules. Use when writing or editing Anki card front/back templates or styling.

plugins.name: anki.cloze
plugins.description: Cloze deletion syntax and generation — {{c1::text}}, {{c1::text::hint}}, multiple clozes → multiple cards, numbering rules, nested clozes, the cloze note type (single card template using {{cloze:Text}}), per-card conditionals {{#c1}}, type:cloze, cloze+LaTeX delimiter conflicts, and Image Occlusion. Use when generating cloze cards.

plugins.name: anki.math
plugins.description: MathJax (\(…\), \[…\]) and LaTeX ([latex]…[/latex], [$]…[/$], [$$]…[/$$]) in Anki cards, mhchem chemistry, and the known conflicts between cloze/LaTeX delimiters and template field replacements. Use when adding equations or chemical notation to Anki cards.

plugins.name: anki.media
plugins.description: Media on Anki cards — [sound:file.mp3], , static template media (leading-underscore naming), the collection.media folder, supported formats (MP3/MP4), importing media via text files, LaTeX-rendered images, and TTS. Use when adding audio, images, video, or generated media to cards.

plugins.name: anki.import-export
plugins.description: Bulk-creating Anki notes/cards from text files (CSV/TSV) and packaged decks (.apkg/.colpkg) — field separators, quoting/escaping, HTML newlines, file headers (#separator, #html, #tags, #columns, #notetype, #deck, #notetype column, #deck column, #tags column, #guid column), duplicate/GUID handling, and export options. Use when generating cards in bulk or sharing decks.

plugins.name: terminal-demos
plugins.description: Recording a real terminal/TUI as README screenshots and an animated GIF with VHS (ttyd + Chromium + ffmpeg) — tape authoring, key-timing and path pitfalls, OCR/ffprobe self-checks, pngquant/gifsicle compression, and a rerender script. Use when a TUI README has stale screenshots or needs a "watch it work" demo.

plugins.name: homelab-server-delta
plugins.description: Use when implementing the homelab server plan — a NixOS module map verified against the pinned nixpkgs, the Compose-to-NixOS rewrites (Gluetun network namespaces, Caddy .ts.net certificates), the snapshot-before-migration gap, and the greps that re-derive all of it. Deliberately excludes what the plan already states.

plugins.name: agent-skill-adoption
plugins.description: Use when surveying, auditing, or adopting third-party agent skills and MCP servers — discovery across the Hermes catalog and GitHub, reading bare-slug registry entries without installing, judging execution-model and trust-model conflicts, and the reasons to refuse a popular skill.
